title: Structured Literacy in Action
author: Science of Reading Classroom
summary: Evidence of Structured Literacy's impact: a third-grade co-taught special education classroom saw measurable acceleration in reading growth through explicit, consistent implementation of fluency, vocabulary, comprehension, and sentence-level writing routines. Students showed an effect size of 0.61 on i-Ready (compared to 0.40 expected for a full year), and ORF gains of 23.4 words per minute fall-to-winter exceeded national expectations. Critically, 41% of students began two grade levels behind; by midyear, only 18% remained in that range. The article details exactly which routines drove this: dyad reading with fluency passages, example/nonexample vocabulary instruction, whole-class choral/partner reading with high questioning frequency, and sentence-level writing with vocabulary embedding.
points: Structured Literacy is not about doing more; it's about doing what works explicitly, consistently, and with purpose.
Dyad reading paired with thematically aligned fluency passages bridges decoding, vocabulary, and comprehension in one routine.
Example/nonexample vocabulary instruction (grounded in Archer's work) helps students refine nuanced word meanings and apply them in writing.
Sentence-level writing as a daily literacy routine strengthens vocabulary transfer, comprehension processing, and academic language.
quotes: Explicit fluency instruction strengthened students' automaticity and accuracy, while structured vocabulary, comprehension, and writing routines supported deeper reading growth.
